summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell activation syndrome, diffuse esophageal spasm, and coronary artery disease s/p CABG presented with itching, difficulty breathing, and chest tightness during a barium swallow, consistent with a mast cell crisis. She was treated per allergist protocol with IV methylprednisolone, Benadryl, and Dilaudid for pain. Serial troponins were negative and EKG unchanged, ruling out acute cardiac injury. Chest imaging showed low lung volumes without acute findings. The barium swallow revealed esophageal dysmotility and transient hold-up of a pill at the gastroesophageal junction. Her symptoms improved over 36-48 hours. She was discharged home on her baseline medications with follow-up planned with allergist and GI, and recommendations to premedicate with antihistamines for future procedures.
